title: POC Gantt and Staffing Check-in - Helix Health POC
summary: Kickoff to align on POC timetable, resource assignments, and benchmark definitions. Agreed on four checkpoints: kickoff, access/infra setup, midpoint benchmark review (2 weeks in), and exec readout (end of 6-week POC). Discussed success criteria (latency p95, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy on eval set), workload sizing, data access, and security gating. Action items assigned for access and initial benchmark run.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Aisha Malik (Helix Head of ML), Ravi Patel (CTO), Sofia Gomez (Platform Lead), Evan Li (PM), Jordan (Security)

00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros and we'll jump into the timeline — I want to make sure the POC gating and who's doing what is clear.
00:18 Aisha Malik: Hey Maya, thanks. We'r— we're excited to see how Redwood handles our search rerank and Q&A flows, especially under our 600ms p95 target.
00:28 Diego Alvarez: Great, can you confirm the three main workloads you want in-scope? I jotted down: 1) real-time search rerank (~50 qps peak), 2) async batch embedding upsert, and 3) assistant Q&A for clinical notes.
00:45 Aisha Malik: Yes that's correct. For QPS, the 50 qps is bursty. Average is closer to 8-10 qps, but we care about the spikes. Also notes: many docs are long — 1.5k to 4k tokens.
01:05 Ravi Patel: From infra side we want to validate VPC peering and encryption keys — we will not allow raw patient PII to leave the VPC. We can provide a synthetic subset for benchmarks.
01:22 Maya Chen: Understood. Ok timeline proposal: 6-week POC. Week 0 kickoff (today), Week 1 access + infra, Week 2 baseline benchmark, Week 3-4 tuning and more runs, Week 5 midpoint readout, Week 6 exec readout + decision. Thoughts?
01:40 Sofia Gomez: That seems doable. One ask — add a quick 'shelf' for a hotfix week in case the KV cache tuning requires deeper changes.
01:50 Priya Rao: We can earmark a contingency sprint in Week 4. Also we'll provide a recommended config: batching window, kv cache TTL, and quantization profile for your model family.
02:05 Evan Li: Can you also capture cost per 1M tokens in the baseline? Our finance lead wants that number.
02:12 Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll report tokenized cost, and break down CPU/GPU time and networking where possible. There may be some estimation error — we'll be transparent.
02:25 Jordan (Security): A few security items: SOC2 type II report, audit log retention, and KMS integration. Also SSO — we use Okta.
02:36 Maya Chen: We'll share our SOC2 and security pack. For SSO we support SAML/OIDC; if you supply metadata we can wire it into the dev console.
02:45 Aisha Malik: For success criteria I'd like to propose: p95 latency < 600ms for 75% of test cases, semantic accuracy on the eval set > 85% (measured by our fuzzy-match metric), and cost delta <= 30% vs current infra for same throughput.
03:05 Diego Alvarez: Quick clarification on accuracy metric — is the fuzzy threshold already defined?
03:10 Aisha Malik: Yes, Evan will share the metric. It's in our evaluation sheet — it's like token-level F1 with a 0.7 threshold.
03:18 Evan Li: I'll drop the CSV and evaluation rubric after the call — link will be in the deck.
03:25 Maya Chen: Great. On benchmarking mechanics — we'll run three bench types: latency tail tests (p50/p95/p99), throughput ramp to 50 qps, and embedding upsert throughput. We'll run them on your synthetic subset first, then on a masked sample of real notes if security allows.
03:46 Priya Rao: Note, long-context tests will exercise KV cache — we'll measure token throughput and per-token cost with and without cache. That will be part of the Week 2 baseline.
04:00 Ravi Patel: About model selection — are you proposing an open model or a Redwood-verified variant?
04:06 Diego Alvarez: For this POC we recommend starting with an open transformer model we know runs well on our runtime (we'll call it model-x in the notes), then try a quantized variant if latency/cost requires.
04:18 Aisha Malik: Can we also try a fallback smaller model for heavy bursts? That would be helpful for graceful degradation.
04:25 Priya Rao: Yes, we support routing policies and policy-based fallbacks — that can be part of the canary plan.
04:32 Maya Chen: Ok let's talk roles. Redwood will lead the benchmark harness (Diego + Priya), deliver Gantt + access checklist (Maya), and be on-call for tuning during Weeks 3-4. Helix will provide VPC peering, SAML metadata, eval data, and a point of contact for infra (Sofia).
04:54 Sofia Gomez: Assigned — I'll open a ticket with infra today to begin peering. We have an internal maintenance window on 2026-01-21, so we'd prefer peering before then.
05:10 Jordan (Security): Regarding data — we need to ensure that the masked sample meets our redaction standards. We'll send a masking script.
05:22 Aisha Malik: We'll also provide a 1k-record eval set and a 10k sample for throughput testing. The 10k will be fully synthetic.
05:33 Diego Alvarez: Good. For benchmarks, expected outputs we will capture: latency distribution, cost breakdown, correctness against eval labels, and system resource utilization (GPU mem, CPU, network). We'll include run scripts so you can reproduce locally.
05:52 Evan Li: On the exec readout — what level of detail do you need? Execs prefer slides with three clear asks: lift & impact, cost delta, and ask (e.g., commit to Dedicated or Hosted with reserved capacity).
06:05 Maya Chen: We'll prepare a one-page exec readout template and we'll co-author with you. We'll aim to have a draft 1 week before the readout.
06:16 Aisha Malik: Midpoint readout: we want to see whether we've hit the p95 and accuracy fences. If not, we'll decide on options (more time, alternate model, or stop).
06:28 Priya Rao: Agreed. We'll present benchmark runs, config diffs, and a recommendation.
06:35 Ravi Patel: One more infra question: do you require inbound access or do you initiate connections? We prefer to avoid ingress where possible.
06:42 Diego Alvarez: We can operate with customer-initiated egress: you'll push data to an S3 presign or secure relay. For VPC we can also deploy a private agent in your VPC that initiates encrypted outbound to Redwood — avoids inbound rules.
06:58 Sofia Gomez: That sounds better. I'll include that option in the infra ticket.
07:05 Maya Chen: Ok I want to capture the gating criteria explicitly — let's read them aloud.
07:10 Maya Chen: Gate 1 (Access): VPC peering or agent and SAML set up. Gate 2 (Baseline run): Week 2 baseline perf run completed. Gate 3 (Midpoint): Meet either latency or accuracy target or agree on remediation. Gate 4 (Exec): Final readout and decision.
07:30 Aisha Malik: Sounds good. One ask: include a risk register line item for long-context tokenization errors — we've seen issues with some tokenizers, and it affects accuracy.
07:40 Diego Alvarez: We'll add tokenizer sanity checks to the baseline harness.
07:45 Evan Li: Are we ok to have the baseline run as a smoke run first? Maybe 100 queries to validate harness before the big run.
07:52 Priya Rao: Yes smoke run day 1 of Week 2, then full runs day 2-3.
08:00 Maya Chen: Great. Any other blockers?
08:05 Jordan (Security): Please ensure we have an NDA addendum for the masked dataset — legal is drafting it.
08:12 Maya Chen: We'll review and sign.
08:18 Aisha Malik: Recap — Helix provides SAML, VPC peering, eval sets; Redwood provides Gantt, harness, and runs baseline. Midpoint 2026-02-05, exec week of 2026-02-23.
08:30 Maya Chen: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the Gantt and checklist by Monday (2026-01-18).
08:38 Diego Alvarez: I'll ping after the baseline harness is in the repo. Expect a reproducible runbook.
08:44 Evan Li: I'll share the eval rubric and CSV.
08:48 Maya Chen: Great. We'll send minutes and action items. Thanks everyone.

(Several small crosstalk confirmations and 'thanks' as call ends)
closing_notes: Midpoint (2026-02-05 30m) and Exec week (week of 2026-02-23). Agreed contingency sprint in Week 4. Redwood will produce an exec slide template. Legal to circulate NDA addendum for masked data.
